   - Modified the `page_pool_get_dma_addr` function to account for the upper 32 bits of the DMA address if `PAGE_POOL_DMA_USE_PP_FRAG_COUNT` is true.
   - Updated the `page_pool_set_dma_addr` function to store the upper 32 bits of the DMA address when applicable.

3. **`include/linux/mm_types.h`**:
   - Altered the `struct page` to include a union that allows for either a `dma_addr_upper` field (to store the upper 32 bits of a DMA address) or an `atomic_long_t pp_frag_count` for fragment page support. This change accommodates the need for 64-bit DMA addresses on 32-bit architectures.

#### Relationships Between Modifications:

The modifications across the three files are interconnected as follows:

- The changes in `net/core/page_pool.c` are directly influenced by the new definitions and structures introduced in `include/net/page_pool.h` and `include/linux/mm_types.h`. - The new macro and functions in `page_pool.h` facilitate the handling of DMA addresses, ensuring that both the lower and upper parts of the address can be managed correctly, which is crucial for the functionality being restored in `page_pool.c`.
- The structural changes in `mm_types.h` provide the necessary data layout to support the new logic in the other two files, ensuring that the system can now correctly handle DMA mappings in 32-bit architectures with 64-bit DMA capabilities. 

Overall, the patch effectively reverts a previous decision while enhancing the code to support the necessary functionality for DMA mapping in a more robust manner.

   - The `page_pool_get_dma_addr` function has been updated to return the full DMA address by combining the lower and upper parts if `PAGE_POOL_DMA_USE_PP_FRAG_COUNT` is true.
   - The `page_pool_set_dma_addr` function has been modified to set the upper part of the DMA address when applicable.

### Relationships Between Modifications

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the removal of DMA mapping support for 32-bit architectures with 64-bit DMA addresses, which led to issues during the boot process when an Ethernet driver attempted to use the page pool with the `PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP` flag. This was exacerbated by the enabling of LPAE, which always set `CONFIG_ARCH_DMA_ADDR_T_64BIT`, resulting in incompatibility with the existing page pool implementation.
        
        Commit message:
        page_pool: Revert "page_pool: disable dma mapping support..."

This reverts commit d00e60ee54b12de945b8493cf18c1ada9e422514.

As reported by Guillaume in [1]:
Enabling LPAE always enables CONFIG_ARCH_DMA_ADDR_T_64BIT
in 32-bit systems, which breaks the bootup proceess when a
ethernet driver is using page pool with PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP flag.
As we were hoping we had no active consumers for such system
when we removed the dma mapping support, and LPAE seems like
a common feature for 32 bits system, so revert it.

1. https://www.spinics.net/lists/netdev/msg779890.html

Fixes: d00e60ee54b1 ("page_pool: disable dma mapping support for 32-bit arch with 64-bit DMA")
Signed-off-by: Yunsheng Lin <linyunsheng@huawei.com>
Reported-by: "kernelci.org bot" <bot@kernelci.org>
Tested-by: "kernelci.org bot" <bot@kernelci.org>
Acked-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Ilias Apalodimas <ilias.apalodimas@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/net/core/page_pool.c b/net/core/page_pool.c
index 9b60e4301a44..1a6978427d6c 100644
--- a/net/core/page_pool.c
+++ b/net/core/page_pool.c
@@ -49,12 +49,6 @@ static int page_pool_init(struct page_pool *pool,
 	 * which is the XDP_TX use-case.
 	 */
 	if (pool->p.flags & PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP) {
-		/* DMA-mapping is not supported on 32-bit systems with
-		 * 64-bit DMA mapping.
-		 */
-		if (sizeof(dma_addr_t) > sizeof(unsigned long))
-			return -EOPNOTSUPP;
-
 		if ((pool->p.dma_dir != DMA_FROM_DEVICE) &&
 		    (pool->p.dma_dir != DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL))
 			return -EINVAL;
@@ -75,6 +69,10 @@ static int page_pool_init(struct page_pool *pool,
 		 */
 	}
 
+	if (PAGE_POOL_DMA_USE_PP_FRAG_COUNT &&
+	    pool->p.flags & PP_FLAG_PAGE_FRAG)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (ptr_ring_init(&pool->ring, ring_qsize, GFP_KERNEL) < 0)
 		return -ENOMEM;
